Technology Briefing · The Hill Report
## Computing Power Is Ranked on a 64-Bit Benchmark
The supercomputer list counts double-precision operations on one dense problem, AI hardware is quoted in smaller number formats, and quantum machines now face a separate federal test that named its final-stage entrants on October 7.
Connor Hill · InsightfulWord · October 15
Key points| |
---
On October 7, Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ were reported as advancing to **Stage C** of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, which asks whether an industrially useful quantum computer can be built by **2033**.
|
---
The TOP500 supercomputer list ranks machines on a single benchmark that requires full **64-bit** arithmetic. The June 2026 leader, LineShine in Shenzhen, measured **2,198.40 petaflops**.
|
---
Hardware specification sheets quote several number formats side by side. One rack-scale system lists **1,440 petaflops** at 4-bit precision with sparsity and **2.88 petaflops** at 64-bit.
|
---
Energy efficiency has its own ranking. The current Green500 leader posts **73.282 gigaflops per watt**.
A computing figure without its benchmark and its number format is half a sentence. The same rack of hardware can be described with numbers that differ by a factor of several hundred, and every one of them is accurate for the format it names.
That is why the public rankings fix their rules in advance, and why the federal government built a separate test for quantum machines rather than borrowing one. This week the quantum test moved into its last stage.
On the tape| Oct 7Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ were selected for Stage C of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, according to company releases and trade reports; three disclosed ceilings of up to $300 million each, and IBM did not disclose a figure.Why it matters: Stage C is the verification stage, in which the government works with each company to test whether its design can be built.
---
Oct 7The Department of Energy committed more than $500 million over five years, including exascale supercomputing, to a $1.8 billion virtual biology data initiative led by Biohub and the National Institutes of Health.Why it matters: federal computing support often arrives as machine time on national laboratory systems rather than as cash.
---
Oct 6Google and Constellation announced agreements covering about 3.6 gigawatts in the PJM region, including an 890-megawatt, 20-year nuclear power purchase agreement.Why it matters: large computing builds are now announced in megawatts as often as in operations per second.
---
Oct 5The Karlsruhe Institute of Technology described its new HoreKa 2 system, built with about 300 GB200 accelerators for €17 million, as having a "peak performance of 33 petaflops."Why it matters: a peak figure is a theoretical ceiling, and the announcement did not state the number format behind it.
---
Oct 2Oak Ridge National Laboratory reported that an algorithm run on its Frontier supercomputer cut the gate count of a quantum circuit from about 2,000,000 to 91,000.Why it matters: classical supercomputers already do part of the engineering work for quantum ones.
---
---
What the TOP500 Actually Measures
The TOP500 list has been compiled twice a year since 1993. Every entry runs the same benchmark, known as HPL or Linpack, which solves a large dense system of linear equations. The rules are strict: the operation count must be two-thirds of n cubed plus lower-order terms, and any method that computes the solution "in a precision lower than full 64-bit floating-point arithmetic" is excluded.
Two figures appear for each system. Rmax is the best performance actually measured on the benchmark. Rpeak is the theoretical peak, calculated from clock speeds and core counts. The ranking uses Rmax.
The June 2026 list, the 67th, put a new system first. LineShine, at the National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen, measured an Rmax of 2,198.40 petaflops against an Rpeak of 2,735.82, drawing 42,220 kilowatts. The measured figure is about 80% of the peak; that ratio varies by architecture and is one reason the two columns are printed separately. It uses processors alone, with 13,789,440 cores, and the list's editors called it "the first China-based system to lead the TOP500 since Sunway TaihuLight in 2017."
Below it sit El Capitan at 1,809 petaflops, Frontier at 1,353, Aurora at 1,012 and Europe's JUPITER Booster at 1,000. One petaflop is a quadrillion operations per second; an exaflop is a thousand petaflops.
By the numbers
---
2,198.40| LineShine's measured petaflops on 64-bit HPL, June 2026
2,735.82| Its theoretical peak, the Rpeak column
42,220| Kilowatts drawn by LineShine during the run
1,440| Petaflops one rack lists at 4-bit precision with sparsity
2.88| Petaflops the same rack lists at 64-bit precision
73.282| Gigaflops per watt for the Green500 leader
---
The Same Machine at Lower Precision
Modern accelerators are built to work in several number formats. Lower precision means fewer bits per number, which means more operations per clock cycle and per watt. Neural network training and inference tolerate small formats well; physics simulations generally do not.
A current vendor specification for a 72-accelerator rack shows the spread. It lists 1,440 petaflops in a 4-bit format with sparsity, 720 at 8-bit, 360 at 16-bit, 180 at TF32 and 2.88 petaflops at 64-bit. A footnote adds that dense figures are "one-half sparse spec shown." Every number on that sheet is the same hardware.
The benchmark community has a measured bridge between the two worlds. HPL-MxP solves the same kind of problem but performs the heavy factorization in low precision, then uses iterative refinement to recover 64-bit accuracy in the answer. On the June results, El Capitan scored 16.7 exaflops on HPL-MxP, about 9.2 times its standard HPL score. LineShine, a processor-only machine, scored 7.92 exaflops, about 3.6 times.
Efficiency gets its own list. The Green500 reorders HPL results by gigaflops per watt. In June it was led by KAIROS, at the University of Toulouse and the national research center CNRS in France, at 73.282, a small 3.05-petaflop system drawing 46 kilowatts. LineShine runs at 52.07.
| 📌 Fresh Signal4The number of companies reported on October 7 as advancing to Stage C of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative: Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ. Trade reports add that Microsoft and PsiQuantum were already in that stage through an earlier pilot program. Stage C is where the government verifies and validates whether each design can actually be constructed.
---|---
---
How a Federal Program Benchmarks Quantum Machines
Quantum computers are not ranked on HPL. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency built its own process instead. Its stated aim is to "determine whether it's possible to build an industrially-useful computer by 2033" and to "rigorously verify and validate whether any quantum computing approach can achieve utility-scale operation." The agency describes the program as "not a competition." Selection rests on written submissions and oral presentations reviewed by government teams, not on a common speed score.
It runs in three stages. In Stage A, companies describe a utility-scale concept; seventeen were named in April 2025. In Stage B, they present a research and development plan; eleven were listed by November 2025. In Stage C, each works with the government to verify that its design can be built. Funding is stated as ceilings, and IonQ's release notes that amounts beyond the first obligation depend on future appropriations.
Other federal money arrives through different channels with different terms. On May 21, 2026, the Commerce Department issued letters of intent to nine quantum firms totaling $2.013 billion, each conditioned on the department receiving a non-controlling minority equity stake. Letters of intent become binding only when definitive agreements are signed; D-Wave reported its definitive agreement, for up to $100 million, on September 8.
The Energy Department is taking a third route. Its Genesis Q competition sets prize pools for systems reaching 100, 150 and 200 logical qubits, and applications are due October 19. Of the up to $215 million planned, $2.5 million is in fiscal 2026 dollars; the rest depends on appropriations.
Where performance figures are published
---
TOP500| Measured and peak 64-bit HPL resultsTwice a year; June 2026 was the 67th list
Green500| HPL results per wattKAIROS leads at 73.282 gigaflops per watt
HPL-MxP| Mixed-precision solve refined to 64-bit accuracyEl Capitan 16.7 exaflops
Quantum Benchmarking Initiative| Stages A, B and C toward a 2033 questionStage C entrants reported October 7
One question for the deskWhen a computing figure appears in a headline, which detail gets checked first — the number format, the power draw or the benchmark name?Hit reply — one line is enough.
---
Worth stating plainlySupercomputer rankings use one benchmark at full 64-bit precision, and they report a measured figure separately from a theoretical peak. AI hardware is quoted in several smaller formats that produce larger numbers from the same chips. Quantum machines are assessed through a staged federal program, and federal quantum funding is expressed as ceilings, letters of intent and equity stakes, each with its own conditions.
---
The short checklist| 1.| Find the number format attached to any flops figure: 64-bit, 16-bit, 8-bit or 4-bit.
---|---
2.| Separate a measured result from a theoretical peak; the TOP500 prints both.
---|---
3.| Check whether an accelerator figure assumes sparsity, which doubles the quoted rate.
---|---
4.| Read power draw beside performance, and look up the Green500 for efficiency.
---|---
5.| For quantum programs, note the stage reached and whether funding is obligated or a ceiling.
---|---
6.| For federal awards, distinguish a letter of intent from a signed definitive agreement.
---|---
---
Replies to this briefing reach a person, not a queue.Connor Hill reads every reply.
Sources checked
Verified October 07, 2026
TOP500, project description, Linpack rules, and the June 2026 TOP500 and Green500 lists
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, Quantum Benchmarking Initiative program pages and Stage A and Stage B announcements
Quantum Computing Report and IonQ, Stage C selections, October 7, 2026
National Institute of Standards and Technology, CHIPS quantum letters of intent release, May 21, 2026
NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 specifications, and HPL-MxP benchmark description
Department of Energy, Genesis Q competition notice, September 17, 2026; Data Center Dynamics on HoreKa 2 and the Google–Constellation agreements

body:
No te dejes, Peter. We’re winning this fight.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter, it’s Gina.
Exactly one year ago today, we launched this campaign.
For the first few months of this campaign, I was totally written off — no one believed we could beat a three-term incumbent. I was a state representative with very little statewide name recognition, and early polls showed us down 10 points.
**Today, because of supporters like you, this has grown into one of the strongest, most competitive campaigns in the _entire country_.** We have wiped out that 10-point deficit and are now leading Greg Abbott in five polls. Together, we’ve built an incredible grassroots coalition powered by over 475,000 unique online contributions and more than 250,000 individual donors who believe in a better Texas.
I want to thank you for following our journey and being part of this movement, Peter. body:
Supporting Susan = Saving Maine

Dear Peter,If you tuned into CNBC’s Squawk Box, you heard something important. Former Senator Joe Manchin didn’t hold back when talking about what’s at stake in this election:“If you lose Susan Collins in the Senate, you are losing the soul of the Senate.”
---
| [CLICK HERE TO WATCH THE FULL VIDEO](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine.-DHPjiiuMVx6bJAQWZbR1w)
---
Joe knows better than almost anyone what it takes to get real work done in a divided Capitol. And he knows that Susan isn’t interested in soundbites, political games, or partisan theater.She is in the trenches for you every single day, fighting for Maine’s working families, delivering real results for our local communities, and serving as the steady, independent voice our country desperately needs.When Washington grows more polarized, Susan stands firm. She never stops fighting for Maine, and she never forgets who sent her to work.Losing Susan’s voice in the Senate isn't an option, not for Maine, and not for the country.
---
| [CHIP IN TO SUPPORT THE SOUL OF THE SENATE](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine.)
---
Thank you for standing with Susan today.
Team Collins

**Americans see this for what it is: President Trump is abusing his power to go after his political opponents in the final weeks before voters have their say.**
I’ve been on the receiving end of this myself. Earlier this year, Trump’s Justice Department came after me and other Minnesota leaders for standing up to ICE’s abuses in our communities. A federal judge threw out their subpoenas, finding they were intended to _“harass, coerce, and retaliate.”_
That tells you a whole lot about how this administration operates. Stand up to them, and they’ll use every lever of power they have to try to silence you.
We need to stand with Ilhan. And we need to back that up with real support for her campaign and the Democrats fighting to hold this administration accountable.

Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Troy Jackson blamed an alleged $40,000 extortion attempt and investigative reporting by The Maine Wire for the loss of his lawyer, missed court deadlines and the dismissal of a lawsuit he and his second cousin filed.
The then-Senate president made the extortion allegations in an extraordinary letter dated May 6, 2024, asking Superior Court Justice Michaela Murphy to keep his case alive even though she had dismissed it with prejudice in April.
"We feel like the opposing lawyer tried to extort us for $40,000 or face public humiliation," Jackson wrote. "When we refused, the humiliation did come, but more than anything it took our lawyer and any legal cohesion we had in the case."
The correspondence, obtained by The Maine Wire, shows how Jackson tried to salvage a lawsuit that exposed his own financial dealings to scrutiny, years before his bid to unseat Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins. The unusual letter succeeded in getting Murphy to reverse her earlier decision, but Jackson and his second cousin eventually agreed to drop the case.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c128e1cb-3585-4404-b40d-d2028c4a13ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jackson and his [second cousin, Lana Pelletier](https://substack.com/redirect/11438f50-11d8-43ab-84ae-345d5f10ef99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), bought the Augusta house from Paul and Jane Godbout for $216,000 in September 2019. They sued in June 2020, alleging the sellers concealed carpenter ant damage, mold and other defects. The Godbouts denied wrongdoing and produced evidence that they had paid for the buyers' home inspection.
Court records examined for The Maine Wire's [August 2023 reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/4e4b8e96-64cd-4bad-b148-0befd69696dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) showed the inspection warned of carpenter ants and recommended a pest specialist. Jackson and Pelletier received the report but did not hire the specialist. In the lawsuit, they claimed they were blindsided by the carpenter ant damage.
Jackson and Pelletier sold the house for $323,000 in December 2021, $107,000 more than they paid. They kept suing.
The Maine Wire's reporting also examined Jackson's federally insured mortgage. Under the terms of his Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loan, he was required to make the Augusta house his principal residence within 60 days and keep it that way for at least a year.
That conflicted with his constitutional requirement to abide at the Aroostook County address listed in his campaign finance filings.
"This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," Jackson [told the Portland Press Herald](https://substack.com/redirect/65422f7d-d579-40fe-989d-9c92d177899c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in September 2023.
Throughout the ensuing ethics imbroglio, Jackson maintained that Allagash remained his legal home and that the Augusta property was for legislative work. His account, which has changed according to the location and audience, has raised questions about whether he ever intended to fulfill the mortgage's occupancy requirement.
On the campaign trail, Jackson has described the house as little more than a place to keep his clothes. During an [October debate against Collins](https://substack.com/redirect/7f67c4e3-4d69-4c09-9b4d-5abbcbbd7d97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), when Maine's senior senator raised questions about the FHA loan, he said he stayed at the house five days a week during the legislative session.
Jackson has not been charged with a crime in connection with the mortgage.
In his 2024 letter to the court, Jackson said the Godbouts' lawyer raised the mortgage problem two years before the reporting appeared:
> "For more clarity, the lawyer representing the Godbouts sent us a letter in 2021 saying that I had violated HUD law when we applied for a loan. He said the home we were purchasing could not be my primary home, because as a State Senator for District #1 my home had to be in northern Aroostook County. He said that if we paid them $40,000 and dropped the case then he wouldn't go to the media. We refused immediately and told them to go to the media."
(For clarity, the lawyer would have had no reason to suspect that Jackson had violated "HUD law," as opposed to violating his constitutional obligation to remain a resident of the district he was representing in the State Senate.)
Jackson did not identify the attorney by name in his letter to Murphy. Jed Davis and Jennifer Bryant, both of Jim Mitchell & Jed Davis, P.A., represented the Godbouts during the litigation.
In the letter and related court records reviewed for this story, Jackson did not supply any evidence of the alleged 2021 extortion attempt.
The defense called Jackson's allegations "false and irrelevant."
Jackson had not raised the alleged demand in the public responses when The Maine Wire first broke the story or in subsequent media coverage. Indeed, the letter is the only instance in which Jackson has claimed that he was the victim of extortion.
His letter lamented the loss of Preti Flaherty attorney Matthew Warner, who represented the couple on a contingency-fee basis. Warner's fee depended on Jackson and Pelletier recovering money, which means Jackson's legal representation -- up until The Maine Wire exposed the lawsuit -- was effectively free.
Preti Flaherty, among Maine's largest legal and lobbying firms, also previously employed [Chace Jackson](https://substack.com/redirect/452e8288-4e63-4fe6-ad7f-1f82a3454e69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one of Jackson and Pelletier's two sons, as a legislative liaison.
Jackson claimed, without providing any evidence, the Godbouts' lawyer later fed publicly available mortgage information to "Republican" news outlets. He then explained why he believed his own firm had abandoned him:
> "The political hit piece was tough, but something I am used to dealing with. What I was not ready for was some of the circle of political foes filing ethics complaints against me. These complaints were all ruled unanimously in my favor, but the law firm that my lawyer worked for had a government affairs arm to their firm and their legal team thought that it was not worth them risking attack by continuing to represent us. He was forced by his firm to withdraw from our case back in December."
Warner's withdrawal motion, quoted in the defense filing, gave a different account: "The plaintiffs have elected to represent themselves, without a lawyer, in this case moving forward." The records contain no statement from Preti confirming Jackson's claim of political pressure.
The ethics ruling was also narrower than Jackson's letter suggested.
The [October 2023 vote](https://substack.com/redirect/ea987599-81e5-474f-81b9-c1ef14549230?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) concerned a complaint by then-Rep. John Andrews, R-Paris, about Jackson's campaign address. Commissioners voted 5-0 to take no further action. The commission lacked authority to investigate the mortgage, insurance and legislative reimbursement allegations. Its vote did not clear Jackson of mortgage or insurance fraud.
After Warner withdrew, the court ordered Jackson and Pelletier to obtain another lawyer or report that they would represent themselves. They missed a Feb. 9 deadline, according to the defense. Bryant moved to dismiss Feb. 22, reporting more than $40,000 in defense fees and costs.
Murphy granted dismissal April 22.
Jackson, in the letter, blamed the missed deadlines on court correspondence he said never arrived after his lawyer withdrew. The court, he claimed, had continued sending notices to the Augusta house he and his second cousin had already sold.
"Apparently, withdrawing also meant not forwarding any of the Court documents or correspondence to us," Jackson wrote. He said he learned about a development in the case less than a month before writing his letter.
His letter listed a different Augusta address in type, with his claimed Allagash residence added by hand. The defendants disputed his account, saying notices had been mailed to Allagash, the address Jackson listed on campaign filings and claimed was his real home during Ethics Commission proceedings.
However, Jackson's bizarre letter, filled with unsubstantiated allegations and outright falsehoods, was convincing enough for Murphy to reverse her decision.
Murphy vacated the dismissal May 21, the same day the court received Jackson's letter. She said it raised questions about whether the plaintiffs had received important documents. She ordered a conference and directed the clerk to send defense counsel a copy.
Murphy, who handled Donald Trump's 2024 ballot-access case, was a [registered Democrat in November 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/28768532-e0f3-468d-b3f0-7f4a03708136?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to voting records cited by news outlets. She is also the mother of Henry Beck, the Democratic former state treasurer. Beck's role hosting a September 2026 fundraiser for Jackson drew criticism from campaign supporters over his [pro-Israel advocacy](https://substack.com/redirect/208e4fe6-6565-40af-9e4a-25cea24f023d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to Drop Site News.
The Godbouts' attorneys asked Murphy to reconsider, accusing Jackson of misleading the court. Their June filing quoted a Feb. 29 email from Warner that challenged Jackson's account of when he learned his case was in jeopardy:
> "Lana and Troy forwarded me a copy of a recent filing you made that referenced a court order from December."
In other words, Jackson's previous attorney claimed that Jackson and his second cousin had not only received the court records they later claimed not to have received, but they passed along those very documents to legal counsel.
Defense counsel said they sent Warner the orders that day. They argued the exchange showed Jackson knew about the dismissal effort months before the court received his letter. They also objected that Murphy reopened the case without giving them a chance to respond.
"The fault lies with Plaintiffs, not the Court," they wrote.
Jackson had asked for the chance to present his claims "win or lose."
On Aug. 30, 2024, he and Pelletier signed a stipulation dismissing the lawsuit "with prejudice and without costs to any party." Bryant signed for the defendants.
The document disclosed no separate settlement terms or payment.
It's unclear whether Jackson ever paid for his own attorney fees or the fees his lawsuit imposed on the Godbouts.

In latest chapter in Troy Jackson's litigious attempt to extract money from the couple who sold him and his second cousin an Augusta home in 2019, Jackson alleges he was the victim of extortion. Oct 15 | | | | | | | | | | | Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Troy Jackson blamed an alleged $40,000 extortion attempt and investigative reporting by The Maine Wire for the loss of his lawyer, missed court deadlines and the dismissal of a lawsuit he and his second cousin filed. The then-Senate president made the extortion allegations in an extraordinary letter dated May 6, 2024, asking Superior Court Justice Michaela Murphy to keep his case alive even though she had dismissed it with prejudice in April. "We feel like the opposing lawyer tried to extort us for $40,000 or face public humiliation," Jackson wrote. "When we refused, the humiliation did come, but more than anything it took our lawyer and any legal cohesion we had in the case." The correspondence, obtained by The Maine Wire, shows how Jackson tried to salvage a lawsuit that exposed his own financial dealings to scrutiny, years before his bid to unseat Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins. The unusual letter succeeded in getting Murphy to reverse her earlier decision, but Jackson and his second cousin eventually agreed to drop the case. | | ---|---|--- Jackson and his , bought the Augusta house from Paul and Jane Godbout for $216,000 in September 2019. They sued in June 2020, alleging the sellers concealed carpenter ant damage, mold and other defects. The Godbouts denied wrongdoing and produced evidence that they had paid for the buyers' home inspection. Court records examined for The Maine Wire's showed the inspection warned of carpenter ants and recommended a pest specialist. Jackson and Pelletier received the report but did not hire the specialist. In the lawsuit, they claimed they were blindsided by the carpenter ant damage. Jackson and Pelletier sold the house for $323,000 in December 2021, $107,000 more than they paid. They kept suing. The Maine Wire's reporting also examined Jackson's federally insured mortgage. Under the terms of his Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loan, he was required to make the Augusta house his principal residence within 60 days and keep it that way for at least a year. That conflicted with his constitutional requirement to abide at the Aroostook County address listed in his campaign finance filings. "This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," Jackson in September 2023. Throughout the ensuing ethics imbroglio, Jackson maintained that Allagash remained his legal home and that the Augusta property was for legislative work. His account, which has changed according to the location and audience, has raised questions about whether he ever intended to fulfill the mortgage's occupancy requirement. On the campaign trail, Jackson has described the house as little more than a place to keep his clothes. During an , when Maine's senior senator raised questions about the FHA loan, he said he stayed at the house five days a week during the legislative session. Jackson has not been charged with a crime in connection with the mortgage. In his 2024 letter to the court, Jackson said the Godbouts' lawyer raised the mortgage problem two years before the reporting appeared: "For more clarity, the lawyer representing the Godbouts sent us a letter in 2021 saying that I had violated HUD law when we applied for a loan. He said the home we were purchasing could not be my primary home, because as a State Senator for District #1 my home had to be in northern Aroostook County. He said that if we paid them $40,000 and dropped the case then he wouldn't go to the media. We refused immediately and told them to go to the media." (For clarity, the lawyer would have had no reason to suspect that Jackson had violated "HUD law," as opposed to violating his constitutional obligation to remain a resident of the district he was representing in the State Senate.) Jackson did not identify the attorney by name in his letter to Murphy. Jed Davis and Jennifer Bryant, both of Jim Mitchell & Jed Davis, P.A., represented the Godbouts during the litigation. In the letter and related court records reviewed for this story, Jackson did not supply any evidence of the alleged 2021 extortion attempt. The defense called Jackson's allegations "false and irrelevant." Jackson had not raised the alleged demand in the public responses when The Maine Wire first broke the story or in subsequent media coverage. Indeed, the letter is the only instance in which Jackson has claimed that he was the victim of extortion. His letter lamented the loss of Preti Flaherty attorney Matthew Warner, who represented the couple on a contingency-fee basis. Warner's fee depended on Jackson and Pelletier recovering money, which means Jackson's legal representation -- up until The Maine Wire exposed the lawsuit -- was effectively free. Preti Flaherty, among Maine's largest legal and lobbying firms, also previously employed , one of Jackson and Pelletier's two sons, as a legislative liaison. Jackson claimed, without providing any evidence, the Godbouts' lawyer later fed publicly available mortgage information to "Republican" news outlets. He then explained why he believed his own firm had abandoned him: "The political hit piece was tough, but something I am used to dealing with. What I was not ready for was some of the circle of political foes filing ethics complaints against me. These complaints were all ruled unanimously in my favor, but the law firm that my lawyer worked for had a government affairs arm to their firm and their legal team thought that it was not worth them risking attack by continuing to represent us. He was forced by his firm to withdraw from our case back in December." Warner's withdrawal motion, quoted in the defense filing, gave a different account: "The plaintiffs have elected to represent themselves, without a lawyer, in this case moving forward." The records contain no statement from Preti confirming Jackson's claim of political pressure. The ethics ruling was also narrower than Jackson's letter suggested. The concerned a complaint by then-Rep. John Andrews, R-Paris, about Jackson's campaign address. Commissioners voted 5-0 to take no further action. The commission lacked authority to investigate the mortgage, insurance and legislative reimbursement allegations. Its vote did not clear Jackson of mortgage or insurance fraud. After Warner withdrew, the court ordered Jackson and Pelletier to obtain another lawyer or report that they would represent themselves. They missed a Feb. 9 deadline, according to the defense. Bryant moved to dismiss Feb. 22, reporting more than $40,000 in defense fees and costs. Murphy granted dismissal April 22. Jackson, in the letter, blamed the missed deadlines on court correspondence he said never arrived after his lawyer withdrew. The court, he claimed, had continued sending notices to the Augusta house he and his second cousin had already sold. "Apparently, withdrawing also meant not forwarding any of the Court documents or correspondence to us," Jackson wrote. He said he learned about a development in the case less than a month before writing his letter. His letter listed a different Augusta address in type, with his claimed Allagash residence added by hand. The defendants disputed his account, saying notices had been mailed to Allagash, the address Jackson listed on campaign filings and claimed was his real home during Ethics Commission proceedings. However, Jackson's bizarre letter, filled with unsubstantiated allegations and outright falsehoods, was convincing enough for Murphy to reverse her decision. Murphy vacated the dismissal May 21, the same day the court received Jackson's letter. She said it raised questions about whether the plaintiffs had received important documents. She ordered a conference and directed the clerk to send defense counsel a copy. Murphy, who handled Donald Trump's 2024 ballot-access case, was a , according to voting records cited by news outlets. She is also the mother of Henry Beck, the Democratic former state treasurer. Beck's role hosting a September 2026 fundraiser for Jackson drew criticism from campaign supporters over his , according to Drop Site News. The Godbouts' attorneys asked Murphy to reconsider, accusing Jackson of misleading the court. Their June filing quoted a Feb. 29 email from Warner that challenged Jackson's account of when he learned his case was in jeopardy: "Lana and Troy forwarded me a copy of a recent filing you made that referenced a court order from December." In other words, Jackson's previous attorney claimed that Jackson and his second cousin had not only received the court records they later claimed not to have received, but they passed along those very documents to legal counsel. Defense counsel said they sent Warner the orders that day. They argued the exchange showed Jackson knew about the dismissal effort months before the court received his letter. They also objected that Murphy reopened the case without giving them a chance to respond. "The fault lies with Plaintiffs, not the Court," they wrote. Jackson had asked for the chance to present his claims "win or lose." On Aug. 30, 2024, he and Pelletier signed a stipulation dismissing the lawsuit "with prejudice and without costs to any party." Bryant signed for the defendants. The document disclosed no separate settlement terms or payment. It's unclear whether Jackson ever paid for his own attorney fees or the fees his lawsuit imposed on the Godbouts. Read more: You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. We talked about my journey from a tough childhood, through my time as a Navy SEAL, building a business, and now serving the people of Virginia's 5th District, and why I'm asking for the honor of continuing that service. Thank you, Catie, for the thoughtful discussion. I hope you'll take a few minutes to listen. == Please Vote Early | Maybe you've seen me at your church? My wife and I attend our church early on Sunday, and then I often visit a second or even a third service. It's Chris.
**There are just 19 days left of this campaign, and we need all hands on deck.**
The GOP has pledged more than $60 million trying to buy this Senate seat.
I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Our strength comes from people like you, and with time running out, we need to show John Sununu that New Hampshire isn't for sale.
**[Will you chip in $10 or whatever makes sense for you right now to help us beat Sununu, keep the Granite State blue, and flip the Senate?](https://substack.com/redirect/79ecf8f5-070f-439f-8b32-d4a0e13e6a2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/79ecf8f5-070f-439f-8b32-d4a0e13e6a2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**I know that in a race as critical as New Hampshire 's Senate seat, falling behind in fundraising simply isn't an option.**
This campaign was built from the ground up by supporters like you. We wouldn't be where we are today without people believing in our shared vision for a freer, fairer future.
But if we're going to defend this Senate seat and keep it out of the hands of John Sununu, we need everyone on this grassroots team to step up.
**[That's why today I'm lowering my ask to just $1 today.](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE $1](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A dollar may not seem like much on its own, but there are hundreds of thousands of supporters reading this message right now, _including you._ When everyone chips in together, even one dollar can make a huge impact.
Right now my opponent John Sununu's backed by the entire MAGA machine and they are outspending us three to one. We need all the resources we can get to fight back. We may not match them dollar for dollar, but as long as we get all the resources we need, we'll have what it takes to stay on track and win.
Everything we've accomplished comes down to the collective effort of this team -- from Granite Staters to supporters across the country who believe in commonsense leadership, protecting fundamental freedoms, and delivering for working families.
With a surge of support right now during these final weeks before Election Day, I know we can hold this seat and get one step closer to taking back the Senate.
**[Will you chip in just $1 today to keep our campaign on track?](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE $1](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you,
Chris

## Paxton Sues Gerber Over Metals
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton [announced a lawsuit](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQBdDTQGdkDwaWwkUauk2bEo3xAFYMRngC7O0jskdIPZr_9f7Xs3-iD36dPnEhw9cY-5XOFIiZ9n7Di-OafihNtFvaB1qZ9i36HiTUQkmhqh4H9gf1GnNnrHStysmopgVZg6p0PhttXV2OVatVDc0DNNKobQsjPHSjhlLn3txxSqpKKQnQFupRWi3R2UYN1WhdpiU5z3EveCamC9MYXvGgvRjikgczM28pKz8y6DLozvMsvjnhfcygeyPErRBvhrhfBYZAEznB8fKDmAmPl1iIMSThV2HRvsQYo8ugy3fjttOH4FPdZFpOC_rwV83_neww8BsAAP__5KuDVQ) Wednesday against Gerber and its parent company, Nestle USA, accusing them of selling baby food as safe and rigorously tested, even though Gerber's own tests showed dangerous levels of arsenic, lead, and cadmium. Paxton said [67 batches of Gerber rice flour](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb8Gd0TwDHEoKLZxN9tuaT3gOUFDTARvYs_frzLRfsHWV_fonvvnY_nAXPJ2_Y138nysddlo74WYqS0PPLhu_Yv6lVqgFmljao-aF1BwllpJbReMnJ-0GBySDyo5PZDXkwN1Bm3NcPOjHR0SUop2CnCJ02qnNTln3IpEcRyyf-G00lZrBeBO-jIGozCFSUe7hiSMopS5thPfiOnAvpbv-qR2ivU-FH9jfnQx_hIwC5j3fT99Pr_oFQqYsXGOhQTMLzMBc6kRi4D5ByRg_qRNvk3lW1Nu1LmQ5HrkKO_EWLoMGL7lWmuS_3pwdlIbM9LotLwggDQQrQyTsZLGiwKdrEYVh-bTY8-l5H6ehFHXO-bys5z_9_Gnh78BAAD__-g_lcU) from 2017 to 2019 contained more than nine times the arsenic level allowed in bottled water. Gerber says its products meet FDA limits and that heavy metals absorbed by crops can't be fully removed. In 2021, an Alaska state lab [found two samples](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LsSnCAYBeCnwQ4HULwUFGnsNm1K5wd-lQTBAdbL22c2-wjpz5w53_n1ml_gvAvrT9hRlXuJc8AreywF03zAXWLIb8wrJo3JYCiYjuhmwURHOaNczmCKO3FuobJKMzvyChXvR8E6wWVbbUoOANg0upXaDoPtlsYawKUZwLKxG2Xl1KeOMy45Z0KMNR8a3TKwuudGLtqSlqF1Jaa6bFjwhrz4J56YahP3yqutlCOT5gcRExHTdV31BXlzYS0x4A27C98oEdMRvTMPEdOG4MtmICERU9t3sh97IqY_GOiXTT9uusPvmKgG_dAlRktN3A8IDjMF73F1YaUWwoopvjP1eKLPNC50QzgfumMBn4mYqqTscTnvXe560rJ1B-f_jS__e_qpxN8AAAD__x3snDA) of Gerber rice cereal over the federal arsenic limit, the suit says. Competitor Beech-Nut recalled its cereal despite lower average readings, while Gerber issued no recall or disclosure. Paxton, the Republican U.S. Senate nominee, is suing under the [Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOkf2YOBRuNiGLttuicZ4AEvGRvaEJH-_IvmE1x8d3XP_3ac7-uDj-hd3Mvxa0hTpWQIxU54OfHGK5UFlpWwpzxSZ8pH8BBI6oaRQ7YQz-5MmjbUzVrpB1WRUP4DsQLW63kwLjW5JAul-abED3fxIPUi00s3Y01x7c-mUVK1SEmC4qZ_GaonO9mpuF-sqLcl5TvnGGzG9sCzhnU7KtzntdTAb81Gq5k8FYwXjB7ApO8r2UXykUi6ughFX8U0SV5P4RgmMTkQqHEhcTrERnm-xE2Mowkdh0b7FkpKrYKyzccfTh-BL11darjv68FnBv33vNPA_AAD__0XCiCQ). The suit says Gerber now posts test results via QR codes on its labels, but its front-of-package safety claims haven't changed.
## Midland Pulls Plug on Flock Cameras
The Midland City Council voted 7-0 Tuesday to [cancel its Flock Safety contract](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOpB3MX-FizR0lzYlMvZyrGQwMntw9_YReYU0o5FGGs18P4_xYTnw9vy2Kxl5z3Hc6DoCiVAad_uWuB0vOp6UJkqONqG0Rx5RYVOAKqAerRM-adQ292ZSvoecDLQ9qgah1vli0EFjK_TT1M1VrfuZdNdBX3maVUc052zuOlBQAyjEvoSumrSyfmrB1fPkM63Is8RUykJCb3vM4RNPSqWLax7MIrIfWfWV4ZDhcF1X-bFLjHea4XAfynB43WKTsAt025V9sJsvHMuncPG1OQ7FGYWOQiitvFmhAitdKWigLRdZQ56M3y8OgY-mzbR6rpbD3wb5L7vT4G8AAAD__8GzhfA) and have the company haul away the city's 73 license plate reader cameras, just eight months into a two-year deal. In February, Police Chief Greg Snow [credited the cameras](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQRp_GdCDPhN_CxW3octst0WAPibXGRvYkJG-_yr7C9p--o3O-rsuVfPDx9p92NvLa0hL5LIFFOC8HvSTF8uBy47xythyF85H8ghr7GnQN3UJW_JOXlipnVu0mqNjAMKHuEbq2uhutLU4TDM5OANCO_cgOXM8AulvHzVbefO5AQwegEacGxsvaanLrALbbVqdazc5Lyo3cWfhFZQvv9OTc2LRXwdxFjqIu_xTOCufzPJt3euSVio-fhcL5I6Vw3r0LFF0tnHcfSbjUW0j2uy60sbxrm6JksqJwrrJxx-lD8KUfVKtvO_nwy5O_dnoa_AkAAP__huN_uQ) with recovering 49 stolen vehicles and nearly $4 million in stolen property. The council unanimously approved the $451,000 deal. By July, residents' privacy concerns had prompted some city leaders to rethink it. Ending the deal now saves the city the $225,500 second-year payment. Midland joins Wylie and Pflugerville in dropping Flock. Dallas pulled some cameras after Gov. Greg Abbott [paused state funding](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L_OozAQBPCngc7INv-OwsU1dLn2SrT2LsGKsZG9CeTtPyWv8PWjn2bm_225gQ8-3v_BToavNS2RzhKImfJywMUplieVO2VL2VFkykfyi5Z6EEoK1S_g2L9o6aBGYyVOqiajxknLQau-qzcztt0gyUKPUk16bYm0RTWiItehJF178-GUVL1SUuupUX9a20lAOyrXrxarThJ6TrnhjZguKGt4pxflxqW9DmZjPkrV_q30XOn5PM9mTdcIz8I-fiKVnj-rKj3vHgNEFJZc2qmIAEyFxdcUzvNbUESxhuQewqXIGRwL2D0KC-4RoGx1NnicPgRfhrHq5H0HH749-Lf_vYz-CQAA___IL4l2) for them in September.
## First Fall Weather Front Sweeps In
The season's first major cold front will sweep across Texas Thursday and Friday, dropping temperatures [more than 20 degrees](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOiOvwSYuXPxNuvztlWixl2CdwchsQvL2J6J7g-t2Z6RPM_N1G24YU1zv_3Ehx68pDysdeyJmKsOGL87r_qD9TmWk4mllKluOg5LKCJAC9ICe45OGDuvgRhks1OSgt0oaBbqrZ6f0RVIYTa-0t963hJM2xoCWVuIEto7uxIEEDSCVsg1c2rGTGMYevJ7GUHWSQuRcGp6J6YX7lN75SaXxeamTm5m3vWr_VepaqetxHM0b55xPt1LXs9ApE_JMRfy-WDj6ROfp8yMF8eEKn1MQU8kri4PoW4CVurWms83MS6qLC9sRU4q76atO3heM6ROC_zre06mfAAAA__-jA4WV) and possibly bringing the first freeze to parts of the Panhandle by Saturday morning. "_Expect wind gusts to around 40 mph on Friday, so make sure to secure any outdoor decorations_!" the National Weather Service in Fort Worth [posted Tuesday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u5CAQhE-DM1vQ_g8INnE2m25oNdAeI2GwoHc8c_snzxVeXKWvVN-_x_pAH3x8_sWDNL-3tEa6SiBmyuuJb06x_KfypGwoW4pM-Ux-BQlDrWSt-hUt-xetHVZOG-lmVZFW4wxyANV31a4BpxlNL5FmhHGzA7jNYCsnKQnA2MrrG6ek6pWSAHOjptZ0Ep0Zle0340QnyXlOueGdmN5YtvBJL8qNTUcV9M58FtH-EbAIWK7rao5PwYiRU_TpLglY7l93Ssg7ZQELZvY2kIDFpuDqLafI9ZdeA3Tj0A5Tc-5nlbU7Lx-CL8MoOvk80IfvMP9W2EvDTwAAAP__RWKCHA). The cooler air lingers through the weekend, with the 80s returning early next week. Ahead of the front, storms could soak West Texas. A flood watch for [18 west-central counties](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGStCAUhE-DGVOAqL8BwZ-YzaYbWk95KFUIFjx15vZbTrAX2KyDru7--vs5PsEHH5cv2NDQy6Ux4lUCEmEed3hRiuXAsmCeMM8YCfOe_KiEarkUXDYjzORPHDVU1kzC9rJCI7teiVbJRlergalpoa7nrtOdFla2KBwohXMvnOhkXXlzx0khGymFUv1D_qsnLcBOnZwbN1mmBVpPKT9oRcIXFBfe6cT8mNNWBbMS7YXV_5kamBoKRIgLhhT8ibeDqeGGYmpIB9mU8i1_CTRTgwspWX4BzSv3pRxo-YWF-A2cIfBPJ6c1p2NZucvewptvKUcflyobu18-BF_ajmmxbODDZxj99dDTqJ8AAAD__2DqjYQ), from San Angelo to Abilene, runs through Friday morning, with 1 to 3 inches of rain expected and up to 5 inches in spots. **Derek,_all_ of those things are only possible because of grassroots supporters like you.** Over 99% of the DNC’s contributions come from texts, ads, letters, and emails just like this one asking regular people for their support.

That is why I want the opportunity to thank one of you in person. Grassroots supporters are the lifeblood of the Democratic Party, and if we take back our majorities this November, your support will be the reason why. If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly. | | ** | | | | | | | ** Thank you for being a part of this, Elizabeth If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

Hillsdale College's popular online course, **" The Genesis Story: Reading Biblical Narratives,"** is now FREE on DVD.

In this six-lecture course, you'll explore some of the major themes of Genesis, including the complex relationship between God and man, and what it reveals about divine and human nature.

"The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text.

The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education.

Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation.

You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph.

This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President
body:
Not everyone is paying attention to state-level races. You’re different, Peter

---
Peter, it’s Barack. More people should be paying attention to the key state-level elections on the ballot this November. Because with so much at stake, _it's hard to overstate the importance of these races to the future of our country_. That’s because leaders at the state level oversee elections. They draw the maps for Congress and state legislatures. They make decisions that ultimately make it easier (or harder) to vote. And with free and fair elections under attack — from mid-decade gerrymandering and threats of voter suppression — we need more state-level officials who care about building a stronger democracy. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee, which I co-founded with Attorney General Eric Holder, fights alongside its affiliates to elect state lawmakers and governors who are on the side of the people — who believe in fair maps and fair access to the ballot. The NDRC also fights to elect fair-minded judges who won’t bend the law or twist the rules of our democracy to help out a political party. **[The NDRC needs your help. They’ve endorsed over 300 Democracy Defenders who are up for election in 19 days in over a dozen states across the country. And they need more grassroots donations to help get leaders like them over the finish line so they can fight for fair maps across the country. ## Social Security Checks Rise 3.6% in 2027
Social Security benefits will [rise 3.6% next year](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQBuCnwZstOINtBoYu3tK1IyJwJFcREwG1lbev3KpP0O2kk_5f3_9xsRdHibbbu3ugaTHbDY-asDUstmZPLlX0X4XaqziqmFPA2ixwmHrBe6Gs8412tNJ1wUREwLFDI2YNfJqkEt3dAA8qRhx5iEouctbLddFuDo57fUU1dmTOPMGFEiAk10MUEkGIBZT3ELVikmOglsvwmWlrd4zplXcsg8-PLpl7a8_KxjcGK4P1OI7BX-vpOP8M1vNksP5y-j9P73NyPXCYe9p8QVeRwdoVE54HpUR1mpnkt4ej9NPT_jnPbuA7AAD__zalerI), the biggest cost-of-living bump since 2023. For the average retiree, that works out to about $75 more a month, lifting the typical check to roughly $2,170 starting in January. The adjustment affects [76 million Americans](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMV2QZzAmFC5uQ5fbbokcMw6zMjiyZ0F5-1W22BfY9hS_9J2P23zznHh__PcbOYl53umsiUSozDUH9qlS-Cosr-K5Uk4LVZlRo72AvkA_-yB80Gx8s7hIhNQ15GAYUVtremhWN3Z-6Oz1bkzQGK_2HijAANRDtxi0XcPu3QMNPSAYPbYRDCHAFfsQMI69MpoWllzaz8y7rBTTKx9U2pC3JrlV5FlV90_hpHA6z7Ot1bePfCic3hyFE-0KJ78cOXih9_ArMO0qW2qKW54np8TVDsrox-Y5_eTlj68cDr8DAAD__4hRdQs), including 7.3 million on Supplemental Security Income, whose higher payments arrive Dec. 31. Personalized COLA notices go out by mail in December or online in late November for anyone with a My Social Security account. Those who want the paperless version must opt in by Nov. 18. Seniors' groups say the increase [still trails](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHO2yAUBeCnwRsWXAO2B4Yu3tK1o0XxJdwKQwQkkd--Sqv_Cf796Oh859dtvzlKlO8_3Ym2h7JnfLeEvWPdW_HkUkP_rNSv6qhhSQe2voMAw6XgUu_Od3rhrtxw2IAIOA1o5byCMEZpOUSrcJHgpNerMOC9MIfWvxdzBD-r2ZllIPvpk0JqCVKJdQxSIUi5gPYewqqZEnhQL3X8Uyj3iCFd5YV19OUcko29PxqbfjDYGGyBsssex8vFUj4JBhv6kst5Mdhc7eQTMtj-6_gXj7ucyzN7bHwy3JfkeCiVg4CZ94g80j1i65wyV_xCVxuXk1ZqXoweYz_TUO3xeFNK1MzMlLifjtK_hf2bx74s_A0AAP__YvWNtQ) the 3.7% annual inflation rate reported Wednesday. _For a better understanding of how much of the increase you'll see,**The Flyover Podcast** today breaks down the various deductions and other factors that will affect individual payments. [You can listen to it here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykz7FuwjAQgOGnSTYi32EnYfDQhY2uHa3DPsNVJkb2FcrbV-0r9AH-X_o-TuFEUmS7vNONveYaNn72wqrcQq9RqHSOX0301Ug615K4a0CD8w7MDlygqPLgYGlMPjMj70f2sBzQzLN1MF79OkdDGed1jbyc89kRObO4vCyQVkA7iv_9gQEHCNYcpgyWEWBFFyPmgxus4SRa2_RZZdMr5_KqD25TrLex-KvqvQ_7twGPAx4bnxttaSqvAY_3mvhbG8HYfLo_pRTp8zJYc7mRlL9e_8l-ePwJAAD__yGCbLw)._
## Trump: Greenland Drilling Set to Begin
President Trump said early Wednesday that "massive" oil, gas, and mineral exploration is [getting ready to begin](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyszAQhJ9GdPJIhxBQqPgbOv9tSkZGB1xGSIx0tuO3zzhFXiD1zu7O931c56unSGn77w90vOY54bNGZMYy17yQjxWXeyF-FU8VcwxYeQYFVmoldTf7hemBs_FNcCsiYNug0_0IylrT6WZ3oeu9Uag1DC3CYNtxNbcwwKpuC1hvG3LvPa10p0EbNV5WbRC0HqBbFljHThiFgTiXy2emxDuu8ZUfWC5LPproduazivafgEnAxDvuFOM7EzDt-cA3koDJh4MSVS6eKScBk9Wmb80oQ04-BsnlfpxyK4gp-hRkpig3X-VBCYuPEr_OmH_LTXHhfFKMVG0vjNoOTz-nDf_R48PBdwAAAP__xlWJlQ) in Greenland, though he offered few details on the project itself. In a [Truth Social post](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0MFqwzAQBNCvsW8J2pVk2QcdCsW39FTo0cjSOlaRLSNtEvL3Je0n9DoDj2G-LtPFxRT364fbyPKSp50eNREzlalmH12q5G8l8rO4WCmnQJUnFNidQJxAT85zvNOkXBvsQoQkW7JgBhRdpzS0q51nVGHo3UxumJ0TgwLwKMCEoLs-hDbalwcCNCAoMZwXUIQAPWrvcRl0owSFyLmcv3PceaUlPfOdytnnrU12ZT5qI98aHBscudx4_Zv-6l-hEoVces-7S-Gz3LajwfHIlWuDI4BR0kgp0EiNfWdkW2w4HjGlWDvTKHHdXPylWv7nQ3eLPwEAAP__5Kt5fw), he wrote that experts say the amount of easily available oil on the island "is far greater than that of almost any land, anywhere in the World." He also framed the island as a shield, saying any future attack on the U.S. "will have to come across Greenland," where American defenses would [knock down drones and missiles](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO2zAQRU8jdTTIsURbBYs07jZtSmFEDe0JRqRAjq3d2wdeICfY-gEf_70_H_MHsnC-_8aNgqYyZzqakCrVuZXIKI3is7J-VeRGRVZqOoMFb5w1bpwxKr9oHrBfQyICOvcU3GUC6_0wuv4RxuV6BX92kRL6aYkeFusXstNk4wWG2HN47znrRgdusNMpuYHAuSuMMUKaxm6wtLKWevpbOOuDknyVF9VTLFsv4aG6t-78q4NbB7fjOE6pfL493ryD216ElWPr4Kb1ue0Gcy7PHKmZDVvjF5nCYu7YzMaZKoqhz11KReWSzS6Ym7lXoiyYV6Plqc3kb4hi_vcxC2VKrK2vYd0PFuHmL91g7xuyfF_VHxZ-BfgXAAD__4Yalpc). The announcement comes four weeks after the U.S., Denmark, and Greenland signed a [security agreement](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZCB3Y2AIHFxCNpdeiDx2m-mTsZHtGXb-fsX-wmYllVSl9_7d17vhwHH7a3bS1ac10lkC1Up5LcmyCYXsK3P9ZMOFUnBU6ooSxxZkC8NqbOU3rco0TnsipL4hDdOMchzVAM1TT-aBNIBXVlo_u34wE_QADy9vDlCphvW1BxIGQFBy7jwoQoAbDtainwehJDmuKXf_E8f6JB8-6U25s2lvgn7WehTR_xG4CFzO8-zso1wcVy9wuaLAZctEMZjo2ppf-9EmDu3OkbIJpd1MaenrCCmbyikKXJqs3XFyCFzGSSi57YbDz2P9pai3xu8AAAD__2jhf10) that expands American bases on the island and mentions "minerals cooperation" without specifics.
## Oldest Known Shipwreck Found Off Turkey
Archaeologists have found what they believe is the world's oldest shipwreck, a [Bronze Age trade vessel](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOkczgyGhcLFNumy7JXLscZiNg5HtBPH3T7z3Ca-8utLR0fl3m25WoiyPv_bFpoY0LbyVyLVynkpyYmNh985S92ylcIqeS50IaFAICvvJuiofnrRtvQnMxF3LBs8jwTDoHtvZXOAO7DUyO22d5g7cpQPqg2ccw8itmIOHgD0SahhPATUT4oV65yiMfaOBvdSUT_-TLHXmEPf04Xxy6dVGM9e6lqb709C1oevKaY18XA1dt5SjL-pHW5VZ1i2zeypvqywPdbfuqbQGUDvbrLwUd3DZq-XY9Z2fvCskPHdAY5uNXzeJUcpwbjQ8Xlbit0P9ZbqPoa8AAAD__5sAhOs) that sank off Turkey's Mediterranean coast between 4,400 and 4,700 years ago, around the time the Great Pyramid was going up. The wooden hull is long gone, but more than 30 ceramic jars and three stone anchors still sit on an underwater slope about 98 feet down near Kekova Island in Antalya. Researchers think the 33-foot ship was hauling cargo along the coast, possibly bound for Troy or Crete. [Watch a video here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQhZ8Gd1gwxj8UFGnc3bQpLRaG68liswLW1r59RPIIaaY6mvN959fX9mUp0vn90x5oakjbiXeJWCvmrSRHNhZ070z1ky0VTNFjqRsImLgUXI6bdZUu3JTtvAmIgEOHRs4axDSpUXa7wVHPIB9op0lrtbhHcAh6ljboZVgeQ0em_ZNCjhKkEroPUiFIucDoHAQ9MiXQU025_53orDuG-EkX5t6lo4tmr_VV2PCDwcpgve-7x3dOTaQFGKwXeUwM1lbDYJWiHdWyKUdf-D8rXnZ63Rndk3sqrhWg5ykEXt_5iZ_Cj0aBOdsT7cldsqV22fjXTTFSmWamxPdhKf7lqv8552XgTwAAAP__Yj-L_g). Several jars still hold hardened black residue, which could be olive oil, wine, or tree resin. Clay analysis suggests the jars were made in [workshops in the Jordan Valley](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2y2yAURlcjdWjgCrApKNK4c9qUGgwXixgJD1xZo91nlPd28Poz5_v5c5_uLuW0Pn-7BS3FMq24t4xEWKdWfHK5od9qoqO61LDkgI0m4KCZ4EyoyXlKH5yk64ONiIBjj1ZcDHCtpRL9bLUBES4AUoz68bh6cH58RGOuSirjjOqTPX2CCyVASG6GKCSCEFdQ3kM0qpMcQ6JSh78lrTRjzEf5YB18WfpsZ6J368ZfHdw6uO37PtBWX-lAKsEdJ9TBzW-ZtoonUGoOjX1NYW1O772if7Ft9acUAysxsm9FY8sZjbW6Fd3KfHGN2AgjB236asN7Tzmnpi-d5M_Fpfy_FP3wy4-FfwEAAP__w4OMPg). One jar appears to have been used to churn butter, suggesting the crew kept goats on board for milk. The find beats the previous record holder, a wreck off the Greek island of Dokos, by [a few centuries](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2y2yAQhZ8GdWhgDfiqoEij7qZNqcGwWMQIPLCyRm-fUfIIabba8_OdX9_Lt0s5ledPt6GlWJeCR89IhG3p1SeXO_q9JTqbSx1rDthpAQGGS8GlXpyn9MFFuSHYiAh4G9DK-wTCGKXlsNpJ3Cac8GFU8Fp_3aN2DzBRGghRmCkOyV5-UkgtQSoxjVEqBCm_QHsPcdJMCQyJaht_11RoxZjP-sE2-roN2a5E785uPxjMDObjOEZasThKtbh88Vx_DGbXqHO_Z9obMpivUAazFNdRl7K2HDr_x8hfpR6F9zW9j4b-xXPtxLfakNPqCldCCH6ia527Z-Wx7iXwGiOnvb3wZDAPzYb3kXJO3dyZEs_Npfy3Mv3n0h8LfwIAAP__YvuUmw). The artifacts will go on display at a new underwater archaeology museum in Antalya opening in the coming months.

Oldest Known Shipwreck Found Off Turkey Archaeologists have found what they believe is the world's oldest shipwreck, a that sank off Turkey's Mediterranean coast between 4,400 and 4,700 years ago, around the time the Great Pyramid was going up. The wooden hull is long gone, but more than 30 ceramic jars and three stone anchors still sit on an underwater slope about 98 feet down near Kekova Island in Antalya. Researchers think the 33-foot ship was hauling cargo along the coast, possibly bound for Troy or Crete. . Several jars still hold hardened black residue, which could be olive oil, wine, or tree resin. Clay analysis suggests the jars were made in . One jar appears to have been used to churn butter, suggesting the crew kept goats on board for milk. The find beats the previous record holder, a wreck off the Greek island of Dokos, by . The artifacts will go on display at a new underwater archaeology museum in Antalya opening in the coming months. subject: MAGA Republicans thought they could draw us out!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF GLORIA JOHNSON, LISA SORENSEN, TREASURER
body:
As you've likely noticed, this election season isn't quite going as they'd planned...

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/0a28850ac720/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363938?e=dc5f639d62)
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
|
---
| |

Friends,
MAGA Republicans tried their hardest to divide us. They redrew our congressional maps in May - a power grab without precedent in our state's history. They thought they could demoralize Democrats, carve good candidates out of their districts, and cling to power. But as you've likely noticed, this election season isn't quite going as they'd planned...
From Memphis to Knoxville and in between, progressive Democratic candidates are undeterred. They're outraising their Republican opponents, they're running strong campaigns, and they're poised to shock the country in November.
Take my friend, State Rep. Justin Pearson. Recent polling shows Justin is [within striking distance](https://us.list-manage.com/k4fzAHDobI0?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) of an upset victory in Tennessee's 9th congressional district. Just last week, the national Democratic Party moved Justin's campaign to its ["Red to Blue" list](https://us.list-manage.com/EAie1NRd1Kt?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0). This is yet another sign that Justin is running a campaign that can actually win, and Democrats and Republicans alike are taking notice.
Days after that news, [Time magazine](https://us.list-manage.com/pgtf4UfLuRy?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) profiled Justin's candidacy, where my friend said it best:
_“This is just another challenge that we are going to face, and we're going to face it together. And we're going to show up more than we have in decades. We're going to participate more than we have in decades because our voting rights are on the ballot.”_
As Early Vote is beginning, it's time for all of us who care about the future of our state and country to stand strong with these Democratic candidates. Organizations like [TN Rise PAC](https://us.list-manage.com/1CgkuraHqGO?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) are doing vital work to bolster Democratic candidates like Justin who are best-positioned to win in competitive races. Polling shows that these candidates can win, but only if enough voters hear their message and turn out to vote. I support the work that TN Rise PAC does and they can use your support. [Learn how you can support the work of TN Rise PAC](https://us.list-manage.com/JmfcGlO0XP5?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0).

Thank you, and let's go win this!
Gloria

Friends --
While my name is not on the ballot in this election, I want to take a few minutes to tell you about my decision to run for Senate in the first place, and why your support remains important to my success -- and the success of Democrats in a number of important races this election.
The truth is, we all know America is _going through something_ right now. We seem to be living from crisis to crisis. But there are certain things that should be really simple:
Like living a middle-class life in the state that invented the middle class.
Like making things in America so that we’re in control of our own economic security.
Like protecting our children from the things that are _truly_ harming them.
And preserving our rights and our democracy so that our kids can live their version of the American dream.
**I ran for Senate because I believe that we need a new generation of leaders that thinks differently, works harder, and never forgets the mission of public service.**
But my decision to run for Senate was also deeply personal to me, and it's related to what motivated me to first run for the House in 2018.
It's about my mom, Judy. She was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer in 2009 — and didn't have health insurance at the time. She had let it lapse after the insurance companies had gouged her for years because she happened to have a pre-existing condition. She passed away in 2011, but that experience — of desperately trying to get her care at the same moment we were filling out bankruptcy paperwork — fueled me to run. I remember the exact moment that made me run: when the then-GOP controlled House of Representatives, the body I now serve in, voted to repeal those protections for people with pre-existing conditions. This story is still playing out today with the Big Beautiful Bill and the healthcare crisis with increasing prices this fall.
Almost a decade later, the Republican leaders, fueled by the extreme wing of the party, are continuing the march to repeal things that the average Americans want. They want to privatize Social Security and Medicare, repeal drug price protections like allowing Medicare to negotiate, then there’s the rights they’re obsessed with repealing: a woman’s right to choose, voting rights, and any possible gun safety legislation.
This next election is critical - taking back the House or Senate is the best way for Democrats to put a check on Donald Trump's power. I am one of the few members of Congress who won their election in a state or district also carried by Trump.
To be upfront: **I plan on spending the next two and a half weeks doing all I can to help elect Democrats running in tough races in Michigan and elsewhere -- like I've done for a number of candidates and state parties over the last several months. But that takes resources. So I am asking:**
[**Will you consider donating $24 or whatever you can to my campaign to help me hit the trail and campaign for Democrats in tough races. We can help them turn out the voters they need to win in these final weeks.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em261015&t=3&akid=2519%2E135344%2EOg2yfs)**

Friend, this is horrifying. Weeks before the midterms, Trump’s Department of Justice just threatened California with legal action, using the debunked lie that noncitizens are receiving ballots as an excuse. | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141450045/653620239/-248329301?refcode=em-10.15.26-all-1-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0NTJjMTJiYy05OWM4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=462gat5TLxiFVFxqjr3A3y59qKCgZJ9LTlLBYIyYKC4=) **Justice Department threatens legal action against California over alleged noncitizen voters**

This is clearly a coordinated campaign to undermine how states run their elections, intimidate election officials, and erode public trust – just as voters are casting their mail-in ballots and are heading to the polls.
But unfortunately, California is not the first state to face threats and intimidation from this president or his MAGA loyalists. Nevada, Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, and countless others have received federal subpoenas for election records.
Trump throws facts and the law out the window. He’s built an entire election-denier movement on undermining confidence in our democracy for his own political gain – and now, he’s using the weight of federal power to do it again with 19 days until Election Day.

| | | | Peter, **Interior Secretary Doug Burgum has announced that the administration is firing up the excavators to begin construction on a massive, 250-foot "Triumphal Arch" right at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery.** They are ramming this gold-adorned monument to vanity forward without final planning approval, without required historic preservation reviews, and while actively ignoring a lawsuit from Vietnam War veterans who are begging them not to destroy the solemn sightlines of our nation's most hallowed ground. Burgum doesn't care. He took to social media to brag about the excavation, **proving once again that he views every sacred inch of American soil as nothing more than a personal playground for the elite.** [**Will you pitch in $25 today to help us expose Burgum’s corruption and hold the politicians enabling him accountable?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/NAs7YQ3OH5orU_DkfnF1nQ~~/AAUS1hA~/_Eb6EhdufQtxsQweLT4fwWaA3Zx6RRdE6xKlm4JFrxDoE3O1BCt60me1AzUWapNG6Vi14W6RQqbTehQSACVNHaWbbi3ws-iaEQY_3XW1-KHBtMrgAb_6pkjNMZttWHC4eMRBGPnQeVwqzrjIb2VlZsTzEoU7b5hpb6VjzPWGag-y9dRzd-wbNKNsZ7pG7pLFW6cNxodx7VConQTa2GuWkZHGpcmtQWyzwgq9qmHLJofPN-WyjORnYidBnCZ0t-Bv) We shouldn't be surprised by this un-American arrogance. The profound disrespect Doug Burgum is showing to our veterans and our national cemetery is the exact same disrespect he shows to our public lands every single day. This is the man who looked at the American public and declared that our wild spaces are simply "America's balance sheet"—**meant to be liquidated for mining, grazing, and timber.** He is the architect behind handing over prime, untouched federal land in the Crazy Mountains to his billionaire buddies at the ultra-exclusive Yellowstone Club, where he conveniently owns a $22 million condo. He is the one rubber-stamping backdoor deals to bulldoze gas-powered AI data centers into the Nevada desert, bypassing environmental reviews and locking out the public. To Doug Burgum, whether it is the hallowed ground of Arlington National Cemetery or the pristine backcountry of the American West, if it isn't making a billionaire richer or stroking a politician's ego, it is useless. At Public Land Warriors, we are funding a targeted, inescapable digital ad blitz to make sure every voter knows exactly how little respect these politicians have for our veterans, our wild spaces, and our laws. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: In Michigan today (health care)
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Look around.
Today in America, there is more income and wealth inequality than at any time in our country's history. One third of Americans spend more than 30 percent of their income on housing and almost 800,000 people in America are homeless. Data centers are popping up across the country over public groundwater supplies with little transparency or oversight, compromising the drinking water and jacking up electricity bills. And we have a president who launched a reckless and unconstitutional war in Iran resulting in increased costs for almost everything in this country.
But there is one issue, maybe above all others, that is never far from people's minds because it impacts every single one of us and those we love in different ways.
That issue is health care.
Today and tomorrow I will be campaigning in Michigan to elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate and one of the major themes of our events, and of Abdul's campaign, is health care.
On this issue, the difference between Abdul and Mike Rogers could not be more clear.
Abdul El-Sayed believes that in the richest country in the history of the world, health care should be a guaranteed right for every man, woman and child.
Abdul was on the team that helped lay the groundwork for the law allowing Medicare to negotiate lower drug prices -- legislation passed in the Inflation Reduction Act that helped almost 2 million Michiganders.
Abdul understands that despite spending more per person on health care than any other developed country on the planet, people in the United States get worse outcomes -- including life expectancy.
Mike Rogers sees things differently. He supported Trump's cuts to Medicaid to fund tax breaks for some of the wealthiest people in this country. He voted against the Affordable Care Act and if elected to the Senate will continue that fight.
Needless to say, on the issue of health care Mike Rogers does not believe what we believe.
I have never understood how people can look at a health care system where tens of thousands of Americans die because they don't have insurance and think that is acceptable.
I have never understood how anyone can look at the hundreds of thousands of Americans who face financial ruin or declare bankruptcy because of medical bills and think that is ok.
In every other developed country on this planet people get sick -- just like we do. But in those countries -- as a right -- they are able to go to a doctor, get the medicine they need, and don't go bankrupt as a result.
There are a million reasons Abdul's race is important. Control of the Senate is on the line, we have a chance to put a check on Donald Trump's power over the final two years of his term, and Abdul is going to be a Senator we can all be proud of.
But if Abdul can win in Michigan it will send a message across the country that candidates who support health care as a guaranteed human right can win in some of the most watched "swing states" in this country.
There’s great value in that outcome.
Republicans know that too, which is why they are spending so much to defeat him.
That is why I am asking:
[ Can you please split a contribution between Abdul El-Sayed's campaign for the United States Senate in Michigan and my re-election to Congress in New York? ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-abdul.jdIzox&refcode=em20261015-12450-P_FND_SPL_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12450%2E2526796%2EE3X0TQ)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-abdul.jdIzox&refcode=em20261015-12450-P_FND_SPL_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=12450%2E2526796%2EE3X0TQ)**
What better way to meet this moment than sending DOCTOR Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate?
Let's get it done.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

**[Donate](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-abdul.jdIzox&refcode=em20261015-12450-P_FND_SPL_MIS&t=1&akid=12450%2E2526796%2EE3X0TQ)** | **[Merch](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/9251?utm_source=em-footer-20261015-12450-P_FND_SPL_MIS&t=2&akid=12450%2E2526796%2EE3X0TQ)**

| Hey friend, Juan here– Chris is an injured combat veteran, an AZ-06 resident, and a registered Democrat. When he reached the end of his rope, he called my office. We showed up and spoke up for him. I work for everyone in this district, so when someone needs help, their party registration doesn’t enter the equation. For the nearly 80,000 veterans I represent, that commitment means answering the call AND fighting for results in Congress. So far we have delivered: 🇺🇸 The Elizabeth Dole Act, now law, to improve veterans’ health care and benefits.
🇺🇸 Four veteran-focused bills passed through the House this Congress, including expanded GI Bill access through the VETS Opportunity Act.
🇺🇸 Bipartisan legislation to tackle the VA disability claims backlog.
🇺🇸 Work to remove barriers to homeownership for veterans, especially in rural communities. Behind every case is a person who deserves to be heard. Chris served our country, and when he needed someone in his corner, I was proud he trusted us.

I was 17-years-old the first time I raised my right hand and took an oath to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic.
I took those words, and that responsibility, seriously every day for the next 4 decades. When I was an intelligence officer. When I was deployed to Afghanistan. When I became an Admiral. And as a member of the president’s National Security Council.
But in all those years, I have never felt as much of a threat to our country, our Constitution, and our very democracy as I do right now. I said I would never run for office. But in this moment, I feel an obligation to step up, serve my community, and defend our country once again.

In 2013, just **21% of Mississippi 's fourth graders** scored proficient or above in reading. By 2024, that number had climbed to **32%**.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d22bfa17-a40a-497a-913b-524adfc1a2c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
During those same 11 years, Philadelphia moved from just **14% to 17%**.
Meanwhile, the national average actually **declined from 34% to 30%.**
_**Mississippi didn 't just improve. It defied a national trend.**_
So what did Mississippi do differently? And why can't Philadelphia do the same?
**In just 9 days, we 're bringing that conversation to Germantown!**
Join us for our **2nd Annual F3 Forum: Faith • Family • Future of Education in America**, where parents, educators, pastors, and community leaders will explore what works--and how we create the conditions for success.

📍 **Brand Mills, 441 E. High Street, Philadelphia**
🎟️ Tickets start at $35. **FREE for pastors, teachers, and Germantown residents.** Caribbean fusion lunch included.
**[REGISTER TODAY-- SEATING IS LIMITED](https://substack.com/redirect/fe023d95-8d77-49f6-ac80-b01ddad14547?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
**If Mississippi can do it, surely Philadelphia can too.**
Let's get to work!

Peter, Roy Cooper here. I’m worried.
We’re 19 days out from the election, and today is the first day of in-person early voting here in North Carolina. Our fundraising is not where it needs to be this close to Election Day, so we’ve set a new goal to turn things around by tomorrow. [**_If you’re able to chip in today for the first time to help us get back on track, it would make a big impact and mean a lot to me._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1673&amount=5&t=9&akid=4578%2E124072%2EGDWpAc)
Here’s why we’re trying to raise $500,000 (I know – it’s ambitious) before tomorrow night:
North Carolina is where the fight for U.S. Senate control will be won or lost. Flipping this seat is a _must_ if we’re going to take back the majority, and that’s why the GOP is going all in to defeat me.
Republican super PACs have flooded this race with tens of millions to crush our momentum. President Trump has smeared my name to his millions of followers on social media. **And now, he’s coming to North Carolina _next week_ to hold a rally with my MAGA opponent.**
**If folks like you chip in and we hit our $500,000 goal, we’ll be able to keep up with the GOP and ensure this race stays competitive. If we don’t meet this goal, we won’t.**
[**_That’s why this is so important, Peter, so I have to ask: Will you give $5 or whatever amount you can spare today to help us reach our goal, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1673&amount=5&t=10&akid=4578%2E124072%2EGDWpAc)

My name is Ron Barber.
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261015-1-b&t=1&akid=11937%2E3935704%2EcGkwKX)
---
Friends,
My name is Ron Barber, and in 2011, I almost died alongside Gabby Giffords.
January 8, 2011, was a brisk Saturday morning in Tucson, when Congresswoman Gabby Giffords arrived for her “Congress on your Corner” event. I was serving as her district director.
It was supposed to be just another Saturday. But in just 19.6 seconds, six people lay dying and 13 others were wounded when a gunman opened fire in front of a Safeway supermarket.
The gunman shot Gabby in the head — leaving her with a condition called aphasia. I was shot in the face and in the leg. I was fading and almost died on the ground. But I thought about my family and tried to keep my eyes open until we made it to the trauma center that saved my life.
**Fifteen years later, Gabby and I still carry the scars of that terrible day._Some days are harder than others, but we can never stop fighting._**
Gun violence is a uniquely American crisis. Gun deaths have increased dramatically in the past two decades, becoming more common than car crashes. Far too often, we see disturbing new reports of politically motivated gun violence when we turn on the TV.
We have the tools to fix this epidemic, but we need our elected leaders to have the courage to take on the gun lobby and defend our democracy.
_That’s why I am reaching out personally:_ The midterms elections are in less than 20 days. GIFFORDS is working to defeat extremist candidates and help gun safety champions win in the most competitive races. But Gabby needs our support to reach more voters.
[**Please, pitch in $3 to help Gabby continue the fight to end gun violence. GIFFORDS PAC is working to stand up against the gun lobby’s extreme politics, and every donation makes a difference.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261015-1-b&t=2&akid=11937%2E3935704%2EcGkwKX)

clean_body: My name is Ron Barber. Friends, My name is Ron Barber, and in 2011, I almost died alongside Gabby Giffords. January 8, 2011, was a brisk Saturday morning in Tucson, when Congresswoman Gabby Giffords arrived for her “Congress on your Corner” event. I was serving as her district director. It was supposed to be just another Saturday. But in just 19.6 seconds, six people lay dying and 13 others were wounded when a gunman opened fire in front of a Safeway supermarket. The gunman shot Gabby in the head — leaving her with a condition called aphasia. I was shot in the face and in the leg. I was fading and almost died on the ground. But I thought about my family and tried to keep my eyes open until we made it to the trauma center that saved my life. Fifteen years later, Gabby and I still carry the scars of that terrible day.Some days are harder than others, but we can never stop fighting. Gun violence is a uniquely American crisis. Gun deaths have increased dramatically in the past two decades, becoming more common than car crashes. Far too often, we see disturbing new reports of politically motivated gun violence when we turn on the TV. We have the tools to fix this epidemic, but we need our elected leaders to have the courage to take on the gun lobby and defend our democracy. That’s why I am reaching out personally: The midterms elections are in less than 20 days. I'm truly grateful

Hi there, it’s Maxwell Frost – congressman from Florida’s 10th District.

I’m reaching out today to explain how critical it is that we elect Sherrod Brown to the U.S. Senate. (If you’re already all in to help Sherrod win in Ohio like I am, [**_you can click here to make a donation directly to his campaign._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141468755/653663909/-1024831887?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6943&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ODJlOTRlNy1hNGM4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AH1D0jBb0p7Xco6BbkevCmXpL0N8ZcXFSwQvIwd0Ohk=))

I come from a family of “doers,” and no one embodied that spirit more than my grandmother.
She went to work in a factory during World War II because, well, that’s what needed to be done. She really was, for all intents and purposes, a real-life Rosie the Riveter.
Growing up, I would go to my grandmother’s house for dinner every Sunday. I would sit and listen to her talk about our changing world and what she had been through. She would often say that contributing to the war effort was the time in her life when she felt like she was part of something bigger.
Around that kitchen table, I learned more about the power of public service than I ever could have in a classroom. I carried those lessons with me for years, even though politics was never something I imagined for myself. Running for office was nowhere on my radar.
**That changed when I became a mother.**
I was at the Massachusetts Office of Child Care Services, working on child care policy, when I realized my entire take-home salary was going toward child care.
I knew what it meant to be the last mom at pickup. To hope your child wouldn’t spike a fever and throw your entire schedule into chaos. To juggle work, family, and the impossible math so many parents face.
And I realized these weren’t just policy issues. This was my life. And it was the life of so many other families, too.
That’s when I knew I wanted to get involved — because my grandmother taught me that sometimes you step up simply because something needs to be done.
Peter, I’ve carried that mentality through every job I’ve had. And today, as the highest-ranking woman in the House, I’m proud to be at the forefront of the fight to make life more affordable for working families.
But the fight is far from being over.
House Democrats are working tirelessly to fight back against Donald Trump’s reckless economic agenda and work to pave a path for hardworking people to succeed — while the GOP majority is doing everything it can to stand in our way.
**We need to win back the House to keep fighting for families like ours — and we need people like you with us.**
[**My grandmother never waited around for someone else to step up. She saw what needed to be done, and did it. I’ve carried that lesson with me, and Peter, it’s our turn to do what needs to be done. If you’re ready to help Democrats take back the House, can I count on you to make a split donation between Eric and me today?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141471199/653665651/1129906623?refcode=10.15.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZTA3NTUwMi1hNmM4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NT2u5b4RobtLo6vFRF8YxSxgp9h7axvcAX_CvHTGGJc=)
